name: mark
description: One press that sets one field on one record: done, pinned, read. A form with a single button, so it works without JavaScript and comes back to the page it was pressed on.

use.when: a person wants to change a record's state where they see it: tick a task in a list, pin a note on its page.
use.not: changing several fields at once, which is the inline editor; or anything that is not the person's own content.
use.with: a collection, a record block, a calendar event, or a record's own page.

type.description: The content type of the record.

value.description: What the field becomes: true or false for a yes-or-no field, a value for an enum.

label.description: What the button says: Mark as done.

context.description: Which record, for screen readers: the record's title. Read after the label.

wcag.notes: A real form and a real button, so it works without JavaScript and is announced as what it is (4.1.2). The button's name carries the record's title when context is given, so a list of ten Mark as done buttons is ten different names (2.4.6). The page comes back where the press happened, with the change glowing like any other.

machine.identify: Read data-record-type, data-record-id and data-field for what the press sets, and the hidden input's value for what it becomes.
machine.operate: Submit the form, or POST prop-<field>=<value> to /t/<type>/<id>/props yourself; the API at /api/<type>/<id> takes the same change as JSON.
